long_description:
Exegete (formerly qualcoder-mcp) is a qualitative analysis application you use in conversation with Claude, compatible with QualCoder. You start projects, bring in documents and transcripts, read them with their codings, search them, and code them with suggestions you approve. You also edit the codebook, write memos, and export your codebook, coding and counts. Each project is a folder on this computer, kept in QualCoder's file format. QualCoder is free software for qualitative analysis, and you can work on a project in either program, one at a time. QualCoder's developers did not make Exegete and have not endorsed it.

Before every change to a project's database, Exegete takes a backup, a copy of the project kept beside it. Exegete runs on this computer and adds no telemetry of its own. On Windows x64, a library it installs for PDFs reports its use, as PRIVACY.md explains. What Exegete's tools return goes into the conversation, and Claude Desktop sends it to Anthropic like the rest of the chat. PRIVACY.md says where your data goes and what to check before you use participants' data: https://github.com/nicotem/exegete/blob/main/PRIVACY.md.

The setting "Tell me when a new version is out" is on by default. With it on, Exegete checks its website for a newer version once a week at most, and when you ask. Nothing from your projects is sent, and GitHub, which hosts the website, records your computer's internet address. The other settings are "Limit Exegete to its small tool set", "Folder for projects", "Your coder name", "AI coder name" and "I use QualCoder on this computer".

small_toolset.title: Limit Exegete to its small tool set
small_toolset.description: With this on, Exegete offers its small tool set, made for models on your computer. That set cannot create a project or bring documents in. With it off, the default, Exegete offers every tool. Settings take effect after Claude Desktop is quit and opened again.

projects_folder.title: Folder for projects
projects_folder.description: Where Exegete creates projects and working copies. The default, Exegete projects in your home folder, is made when needed. A sync service that keeps this folder copies your projects off this computer and can leave a damaged copy. With this empty, Exegete does not start.

coder_name.title: Your coder name
coder_name.description: The name your own codings carry, kept apart from the AI's. Exegete gives it to each project it creates. If it is empty, the default, Claude asks for it at each new project. It must differ from the AI coder name.

ai_coder_name.title: AI coder name
ai_coder_name.description: The name under which Exegete stores Claude's work, kept apart from yours. Each project Exegete creates gets it. If it is empty, the default, Claude asks for it when a project first needs one. A model's name here lets you compare models' work.

i_use_qualcoder.title: I use QualCoder on this computer
i_use_qualcoder.description: With this on, Exegete adds notes that matter if you open projects in QualCoder. With it off, the default, Exegete adds them only when it finds signs of QualCoder in the project or on this computer. It always checks whether QualCoder has a project open.

update_check.title: Tell me when a new version is out
update_check.description: With this on, the default, Exegete checks its website for new versions once a week at most, and when you ask. Nothing from your projects is sent. GitHub, which hosts the website, records your computer's internet address. With it off, Exegete itself makes no connection.
